brief: #66's litter lands on ROAD and SIDE too — the street trees' leaves cross the footway and lie on the road (the surprise of #66) — and the only thing that clears paving is the courtyard's pre-dawn sweeper (`a.broom`), which never walks the cross street. So a street heap lasts until decay or snow while the courtyard's is scuffed clear each dawn. Connect the street to a clearing: either extend the sweeper's round to the cross street footway on some mornings, or let the road's litter be cut by the cyclists and walkers that already use it at a higher rate than grass, or both — pick the one that reads from the wide shot and say why. Also confirm the footway/road litter is DRAWN (drawLitter's tile check) and not only raised.
successLooksLike: An autumn-morning crop pair (day 16, 07:00 and 12:00) of the cross street shows a heap on the road that is visibly cut by midday on HERE and not on HEAD; litter-year.mjs prints per-tile-class sums (GRASS/PATH/SIDE/ROAD) and the ROAD sum on HERE falls faster than HEAD's while the courtyard sums are identical; ground rebuild count unchanged; motion gate PASS; the sweeper's courtyard round is unchanged in timing.
avoid: Do not add a second sweeper agent under laneCap. Do not decay ROAD litter faster by constant — the clearing must be something a viewer can watch happen.
